questions.stem: Why does a bouncing ball reach a lower height with each bounce?

options.text: Energy is destroyed during each bounce
Some energy is transferred to thermal and sound energy stores during each bounce
Gravity gets stronger with each bounce
The ball gains mass with each bounce

questions.explanation: During each bounce, some kinetic energy is transferred to thermal energy (deformation of the ball) and sound energy. This means less energy is available to convert back to gravitational potential energy, so the ball does not reach the same height.

questions.stem: Why is a perpetual motion machine impossible?

options.text: Energy dissipation means useful energy always decreases over time

questions.explanation: A perpetual motion machine would need to run forever without any energy input. This is impossible because energy is always dissipated (spread out as thermal energy through friction, air resistance, etc.), so the useful energy available decreases over time.
